headline: High: CrewAI’s default write/network/browser capabilities can conflict with Taipy workflows and create unsafe cascading actions; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers, so Taipy outputs could be bridged through files or UI artifacts if the orchestrator passes them along. Taipy exposes no explicit isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF CrewAI ingests Taipy-generated files or browser-rendered content as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic parsing of Taipy output as prompts
Add a provenance prefix to all inter-agent messages
Review any browser-scraped content before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, with broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive inputs can leave the host. Taipy shows no network egress and no touched data classes, but if it receives CrewAI-produced files in a shared workspace, leakage can still occur through CrewAI’s outbound calls. The pairwise path is plausible in default-style setups, not proven.
conditions: IF CrewAI is given secrets or sensitive crew data
IF Taipy reads files from the same workspace that CrewAI writes to
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Use separate service accounts and directories
Turn off unnecessary CrewAI tool integrations
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress in the host working directory. Taipy is a data-engineering framework that may also operate on shared project files, but its write scope is not explicit in the profile; uncertainty therefore escalates. If both touch the same mutable workspace, conflicting writes and race conditions can corrupt state or outputs.
conditions: IF Taipy writes to the same project directory that CrewAI uses
IF both agents mutate shared files without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared artifacts
Snapshot files before each agent run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and act through configured integrations, while Taipy is a data-engineering layer that may consume those outputs downstream. If Taipy treats CrewAI-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect pipelines or actions. Because Taipy’s verification controls are not documented here, the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes CrewAI outputs without validation
IF CrewAI tool results are used to trigger Taipy jobs or transformations
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Taipy acts
Validate schemas on all CrewAI outputs
Require explicit approval for downstream jobs
Log and diff intermediate artifacts
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while Taipy’s profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency constraints. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The Taipy side is not cited for a specific violation because its profile lacks relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into CrewAI-managed crew inputs
IF Taipy is deployed under a stricter retention or residency policy than CrewAI
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared inputs
Document retention and deletion expectations
Restrict CrewAI secrets to runtime injection
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
